sources.role_in_paper: Individual-level data for all models (pp. 679-685; Online Appendix tables A1-A3): entrepreneurial activity (nascent or established owner-manager), female, age and age squared, post-secondary degree, labour-force restriction and employment status, perceptions (skills, fear of failure, knows entrepreneur; supplementary model 3), owner subsample outcomes (no-better-choices motive, business size from current jobs, growth aspiration from expected jobs in five years, product new to all customers, technology less than five years old), ownership share (sole owner), business age (first year of payments to owners); survey-level control 'social status of entrepreneurship' (country-year mean of the status item, p. 683-684). The article does not name the GEM release or distributor.

sources.licence_terms: ICPSR Terms of Use (TermsOfUse.html, agreed by the user on 2026-10-27): research/statistical use only; no re-identification; no redistribution without ICPSR written agreement except among authorized users at member institutions; cite the dataset; report publications to ICPSR bibliography; restriction on sharing with listed countries of concern. Implication for this study: keep data inside the study folder; never copy to reader staging; implementers may receive derived numeric extracts only within the project.
sources.release_vintage: ICPSR 20320 V6, 2022-07-12 (data/codebook added 2021-04-12; harmonized file version 4.01 per PI codebook dated 2020-04-01). Paper (published 2015, survey years 2001-2008) used an unnamed GEM release; necessarily an earlier vintage (GEM public annual files and/or ICPSR V1-V3). Harmonization, age imputation and transformed variables in V6 may differ from what the author used.
sources.status_reason: All 143 paper country-years are present and nearly all needed variables exist, but (1) the status item NBSTATUS (input to the social-status control) has no valid responses in survey years 2001 and 2002 for any country; (2) GEMWORK and GEMEDUC have no valid responses for France 2003, a paper survey-year; see registry/validation/README.md.
sources.integrity: SHA-256 of all 7 files equal the inventory in data/supplied/supplied_sources.json; MD5 of Data.sav, Codebook-ICPSR.pdf and Codebook-PI.pdf equal the ICPSR manifest. Manifest lists other formats (dta, rda, stc, tsv, txt, setup files) and 20320-descriptioncitation.pdf that are not in the bundle; not needed (the .sav suffices; the citation page is present as HTML).
sources.notes: Read-only; not copied. Loads in pyreadstat 1.3.3 and R haven 2.5.5 with identical shape (2,796,985 x 97) and identical fingerprints on 10 variables (WEIGHT sums differ only at 1e-6 float rounding). Missing values are not declared as SPSS user-missing; they are system-missing plus labelled codes (e.g. 8/9, 9999, 999999...) documented in value labels.

sources.role_in_paper: Paid leave for mothers in FTE weeks (p. 681-682, footnote 6): 'Ray, 2008' and 'Ray, Gornick, and Schmitt, 2010' cited for weeks of full-time-equivalent paid leave (duration x wage replacement rate), 21 countries.
sources.provider: Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR), Washington DC; archived copies from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine
sources.url_or_query: Original URLs http://www.cepr.net/documents/publications/parental-app_2008_09.pdf (Ray 2008, 'A Detailed Look at Parental Leave Policies in 21 OECD Countries', Sept 2008), .../parental_2008_09.pdf (Ray, Gornick & Schmitt 2008, 'Parental Leave Policies in 21 Countries: Assessing Generosity and Gender Equality', CEPR report), .../parental-summary-2008-09.pdf (one-page summary); retrieved as raw archived bytes via https://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<original URL> (captures 2008-10-23 and 2010-10-17)
sources.licence_terms: Publicly released CEPR reports; no licence statement found; documentary use. The 2010 Journal of European Social Policy article (Ray, Gornick & Schmitt 2010) is paywalled and was not acquired; the 2008 CEPR report is its public working-paper version.
sources.release_vintage: Ray (2008) and the 2008 CEPR report match the paper's cited Ray (2008); the JESP 2010 article version (cited) not acquired - possible minor revisions between versions.
sources.status_reason: Ray 2008 obtained; JESP 2010 article version not obtained (paywalled). Direct cepr.net download blocked by a Cloudflare browser challenge (not bypassed); archived originals used. Covers 21 of the paper's 24 countries; Czech Republic, Iceland and Poland do not appear in either report (text check); for these the ILO and OECD sources are the only acquired leave sources.
sources.notes: These are source publications containing printed policy parameters; they are permitted public primary records (not the focal article). The paper says it 'used multiple sources to create an FTE paid-leave database' with policy changes for 8 countries lagged one year; this construction is not reproducible from a single file.

sources.role_in_paper: Paid leave for mothers (p. 681-682): 'ILO, 2012, Maternity protection database' (ILO Conditions of Work and Employment Programme, TRAVAIL), used as one of multiple sources for the FTE paid-leave database.
sources.provider: International Labour Organization (ILO) TRAVAIL legal databases, Maternity protection; archived copies from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine
sources.url_or_query: Cited URL http://www.ilo.org/travaildatabase/servlet/maternityprotection now 404; database discontinued at ilo.org/dyn/travail (404). Retrieved archived country reports: https://web.archive.org/web/<ts>id_/http://www.ilo.org:80/dyn/travail/travmain.sectionReport1?p_lang=en&p_countries=<ISO2>&p_sc_id=2000&p_year=<2009|2011>&p_structure=3 (fallback for 2011: ...&p_print=Y capture of 2016-03-12)
sources.licence_terms: ILO web content; documentary use; no login.
sources.release_vintage: Database editions labelled 2009 (captures 2010-01 and 2012-08) and 2011 (captures 2012-08-25; Belgium, Ireland, Netherlands from 2016-03-12 print captures). The paper cites ILO 2012 (consistent with the 2011 edition as online in 2012).
sources.status_reason: Substantive 2011-edition reports for 21/24 countries (missing Canada, France, Poland: no archived capture). 2009-edition reports substantive for 20/24 (Czech Republic, Greece, Poland captures are empty shells; Portugal not captured). Poland has no substantive report in either edition.
sources.notes: Archived HTML pages saved unmodified. Each page includes ILO site navigation text; country content follows the country list.

sources.role_in_paper: OECD (2012a) Family Database: (a) paid leave for mothers (cited with Ray and ILO; p. 681-682); (b) state childcare spending, % of GDP spent on childcare services for children under five, 'published in 2005 and again in 2007; information for missing years was imputed' (p. 682, footnote 9); (c) fertility rate (p. 684). Also alternative-control candidates: women's part-time share (LMF1.6), women's share of managers (LMF1.6, 2010+ only), enrolment (PF3.2; footnote 9 alternative).
sources.provider: OECD, Directorate for Employment, Labour and Social Affairs, OECD Family Database
sources.licence_terms: OECD terms and conditions (oecd.org/termsandconditions): OECD data may be used and reproduced with attribution (CC BY 4.0 for OECD data since 2024); no login.
sources.release_vintage: Current vintage (files cover up to 2021-2025). Paper used the 2012 vintage. Differences: PF3.1 time series is total public spending on early childhood education and care (childcare plus pre-primary), not 'childcare services' alone, and is a revised series rather than the 2005/2007 publication points; PF2.5 time series gives weeks of paid leave by year but no historical payment rate, so FTE weeks cannot be computed from it alone; PF2.1 gives current (2025) payment rates/FRE only; SF2.1 fertility series revised.
sources.notes: Old cited URLs (www.oecd.org/els/family/...) return 404 and the OECD landing page returned 403; webfs.oecd.org files downloaded without login. France's PF2.5 Total_paid entries are text (parity-dependent), not numeric.

sources.role_in_paper: Sourced alternative/complement for state childcare spending (p. 682): SOCX public expenditure on family, early childhood education and care (TP521) and maternity/parental leave (TP512), % GDP, annual. The 2012 Family Database childcare indicator was derived from SOCX plus education spending data.

sources.licence_terms: UNDP publications, freely downloadable; documentary use with attribution; no login.
sources.release_vintage: Exactly the six cited reports (HDR 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007/2008, 2009, 2010). Statistical tables in each report generally refer to data about two years before the report year (per HDR conventions); mapping report to survey year is an implementer decision.
sources.status_reason: PDFs obtained for all six cited reports and all 24 countries appear in each. Text layer: 'GDP index' and 'legislators, senior officials and managers' labels present in 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007/8 and 2009 reports; absent from HDR 2010 (which replaced the GDP index by a GNI-based income index and the GEM by the Gender Inequality Index). Values are printed tables in PDFs requiring extraction.
sources.notes: Machine-readable historical HDR tables (e.g. Excel annex tables for 2004-2009) were not located; HDRO's current time series do not include the old GDP index or the female-managers share.
